title: DynVec: An End-to-End Framework for Efficient Vector-Dataflow Execution
problem: HLS tools struggle with vectorization and dynamic scheduling for irregular workloads due to unknown memory access patterns and control flow divergence at compile time.
motivation: Enable efficient hardware acceleration of irregular kernels by combining compile-time and runtime parallelism optimization through vectorization and dynamic dataflow scheduling.
method: DynVec: MLIR-based context-aware vectorizer generating vector-dataflow execution graphs with high-level elastic units supporting built-in vectorization. Integrates dynamic scheduling with automatic vectorization to exploit runtime parallelism.
key_novelty: First unified vector-dataflow framework integrating vectorization and dynamic scheduling for irregular kernel acceleration.
contributions: Significant speedup over state-of-the-art HLS implementations
Superior performance vs hybrid accelerators with separate vectorization/dynamic support
Context-aware vectorizer identifying vectorizable operations in irregular code
Bottom-up type-safe composition of vector and scalar operations
MLIR-based framework preserving kernel structural hierarchy
baselines: Hybrid accelerators with separate vectorization/dynamic scheduling
limitations: Evaluated on regular and irregular applications; HLS-specific, compiler-focused approach.
primary_theme: Vector-dataflow framework with compile-time and runtime parallelism optimization
